newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Hillary Clinton says new S.Africa a country of hope.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton says new S.Africa a country of hope.

text.p: U.S. First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton said on Friday that South Africa was a country of hope before she and her daughter Chelsea left Cape Town on the next leg of their African tour.

"Though I am leaving South Africa I will take with me forever all that I have seen here. I saw a country coming to life with the spirit of hope, opportunity and reconciliation," Mrs. Clinton said in a statement before leaving for Zimbabwe.

"Everyone I met from Archbishop (Desmond) Tutu and the members of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission to the students at the University of Cape Town, convinced me that South Africans are committed to this historic mission," she added.
Mrs Clinton said while she had seen for herself South Africans building a future together, she had also been reminded of its turbulent past under apartheid.
"In talking about South Africa's future it was impossible not to be moved by its past," she said referring to a visit in Johannesburg's sprawling Soweto township.

While there, she saw the memorial of Hector Peterson, a teenage boy among the first to die in police gunfire during a huge demonstration against white rule. Nearly 700 people died in the violence that followed -- most shot by police.
"At Hector Peterson's memorial, at a tree-planting at Cowley House, and in a cell on Robben Island, I was reminded all too clearly of the bloody markers on this country's road to freedom.
"I was also reminded of the importance of preserving the memory of that time so that it may inspire future generations to continue the hard work of building the new South Africa," Mrs. Clinton said.
President Bill Clinton's wife said she hoped ties between the two countries would be strengthened by her visit.

"I am proud of the close ties between the United States and South Africa. After my visit I am confident that they will grow even stronger," she said thanking President Nelson Mandela for an "unforgettable" visit.
Mandela took Mrs. Clinton and her 17-year-old daughter on a personal tour of the prison on Robben Island on Thursday where he was jailed for 18 years of his 27 years in jail for opposing apartheid.
Mrs. Clinton's African six-nation safari is her ninth solo trip outside the United States. The two-week goodwill mission includes Zimbabwe, Uganda, Tanzania and Eritrea.
